newsitem.title: UK: IRA bomb suspect granted bail by British court.
newsitem.headline: IRA bomb suspect granted bail by British court.

text.p: IRA bomb suspect Roisin McAliskey, allowed to leave prison last week to have her baby in a London hospital, was granted bail on Tuesday.
McAliskey and her newborn daughter Loinnir will not have to return to prison and can now be moved to a specialist mother and baby unit, the High Court ruled.

The 25-year-old prisoner had been held in Britain's high security Holloway prison since last year pending extradition to Germany for questioning about an Irish Republican Army mortar attack at a British army base in Osnabrueck.
McAliskey was allowed limited bail to move to hospital three days before the baby was born in a London hospital on May 26.

Supporters have argued that there was no reason why McAliskey should not be granted unconditional bail and have been fiercely critical of the conditions in which she had been held in prison. The prison service denied she was being harshly treated.

Her mother, the Irish republican firebrand Bernadette McAliskey, nee Devlin, said last week that security officers even accompanied her daughter to ante-natal classes in prison where the most intimate issues were being discussed.

"There is not one single supportable shred of evidence to indicate that she has the most minimal knowledge of that offence", McAliskey said of accusations that her daughter was involved in the Osnabrueck bombing last June.
She said the German evidence had now been reduced to one small piece of 'Cellophane' (adhesive tape) in a rubbish bag that they claim has her daughter's fingerprints on it.

McAliskey was granted bail as multi-party peace talks on Northern Ireland resumed in Belfast. Sinn Fein, the IRA's political wing, remains excluded from the talks until the IRA declares a credible ceasefire.
